doc.title: Bobby Militello interviewed by Monk Rowe, Buffalo, New York, October 14, 2002

title: Maynard's stamina; the 1981 phone call from Dave Brubeck
summary: After Maynard, Florida and a fusion band, Dave Brubeck phoned him for an audition, having noted his Sugar Bush flute solo of 1977.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: How does he keep up physically with what he does?

He’s very into his yoga and his thing that he does that way and all that stuff. And he’s a road rat. Road rats tend to be able to deal with the road and the turmoils and the physical stresses and that kind of stuff. You know I’m a heavy guy and everything else and our schedule with Dave is busy as hell. And yet you tend to deal with it. You figure it out and you make it work. He’s done well. I mean he’s in pretty good shape. He’s gained a little weight but — the last time I saw him I said, “It looks good on ya, man.” He’s always been on diets and done things and stuff like that. But he seemed to be in pretty good shape. But getting the gig with Maynard and then leaving Maynard, I did a gig for a year in Florida after I left Maynard with Dick Fadele, a local guy, and again did an album with him that’s great and a bunch of things, and then after that came back and started a fusion band in Buffalo. And about two years into having a fusion band, Rick James used to come to see me all the time and bring his whole band in, because he said, “Listen to the precision of these guys playing,” I mean a quintet sounds like freaking a big band. Because we’d write everything out. Everything was very precise. During that period of time is when I got a phone call from Brubeck. 1981 actually. And I remember being in the house and my wife is in the other room cooking something and I get a call on the phone. “Hi is Bobby Militello there?” I says, “Yeah.” He says, “This is Dave Brubeck.” I said, “Yup, who is this?” One of those type of things. He says, “This is Dave Brubeck, calling you from New York.” “Okay what do you want?” I’m still figuring something is coming at me. “Well we want you to come and audition for the band if you would, in New York, next week. I need a horn player.” I says, “Oh yeah, how’d you get my name?” He says, “Well you remember playing the Sugar Bush Jazz Festival in 1977?”

I says, “Yeah, with Maynard Ferguson?” All of a sudden I’m realizing there’s some truth in who this is on the phone. And he says, “Well you played that flute solo,” he says, “well my wife was out in the crowd and she heard you and came back to get me.” I came out and only heard the last 30 seconds, maybe minute of your solo, but twenty thousand people stood up and cheered when you finished. And he said, “That sort of said something. But my wife said you were a phenomenal player. So we wrote your name down in the book that day, our day book. We went back, went through seven or eight years of day books until we found your name, called up Maynard and asked him where you were and he gave us your number in Buffalo.” I says, “All right.” He says, “So would you want to come?” I says, “Yes.” Went there, he sent me a book of tunes, new tunes that they were doing of course, they weren’t doing all the old quartet stuff. But when I go to do the audition they were preparing for a gig they had to do in New York and who is there is Joe Morello and Eugene Wright.
